$comment: Schema v2. Version-agnostic pattern database for scan_notebook.py. Each entry carries a LIFECYCLE ({introduced, deprecated, superseded, removed}) as strict version strings (parsed by mesa_versions.parse_version; prose is a hard load-time error). The scanner COMPUTES a status at the --target: not-yet-introduced (API newer than target) > removed (errors at target) > deprecated (warns at target) > legacy (silently superseded, slated for removal) > current. There is no materialized status. Lifecycle stamps are empirically verified (see scripts note): probed on mesa 2.3.4/3.0.3/3.1.5/3.2.0/3.3.1/3.4.2/3.5.1. Mesa-4 removals use removed:'4.0.0a0' so a 4.0.0a0 target computes them removed. Field semantics: kind = api|prose|install (default api). judge:true = the pattern cannot self-certify, so the hit NEVER hard-blocks the zero gate (a computed removed/deprecated/legacy/not-yet-introduced is downgraded to judge, with the computed status kept in the note). judge_when controls whether it ALSO surfaces at a target where the API is simply current: 'always' (default) for entries carrying a real check a human must run on correct code (ContinuousSpace keep rule, cell-space random=self.random / base-class mobility, batch_run checklist); 'stale' when the flag exists only to protect the ambiguous downgrade direction (model.rng, run_for, to_list, model.steps) — announcing those at a target where they are current is pure noise (measured: 46% of all judge items on four finished notebooks). applicable_min/applicable_max = the entry's CONCERN only exists in [min,max) (opposite polarity to API existence; e.g. reserved-name assignment only harms >=3.0.0). by_target = [{min,max,replacement,note,status}] band overrides, first match wins (min incl, max excl); an explicit band status is honored verbatim — status:'judge' surfaces the hit WITHOUT blocking the zero gate (for prose whose kwarg may belong to another library), status:'current' suppresses. multiline:true = the scanner additionally reruns the entry's patterns on a newline-flattened, comment-blanked copy of each code cell, so a kwarg pattern still fires when its call spans lines (super().__init__( / def __init__( split across lines). explain:true = comment-parity: when the entry's API is current at the target, each matching code line must carry a comment on or directly above it, else the scanner emits an `uncommented-new-api` judge item (migration-inserted modern constructs must be as well explained as the rest of the notebook; silence is fine where it matches the notebook's density). replacement may contain {TARGET}. For old-API entries replacement is the forward fix; for anachronism (not-yet-introduced) entries it is the target-era form (the downgrade/don't-overshoot work list). Every hit is fixed or explicitly judged a false positive in the report — never skipped silently. When Mesa releases a new version, extend this file together with version-catalog.json and version-history.md (see SKILL.md 'Maintaining the version history').

entries.replacement: On a mesa.discrete_space.Network the graph is ALIASED (grid.G is model.G): mutating G directly (G.remove_edge/add_edge/remove_node) desyncs cell neighborhoods from the graph — the model runs but is silently wrong (version-history.md §6.3). Route connectivity changes through the grid: grid.remove_connection(cell_a, cell_b) / grid.add_connection(...) / grid.remove_cell(cell). Reads (G.degree, G.has_edge, G.number_of_edges, G.neighbors) are fine.
entries.note: judge:true, applies_to:both — also fires on textual-solution PROSE that instructs `model.G.remove_edge()` (a real miss: markdown hints go stale/dangerous the same way code does). On a LEGACY mesa.space.NetworkGrid target, direct G mutation is the normal idiom — judge by which space the file uses. Only mutation methods match; graph reads are not flagged.
